observable_features: A central sculptural group with diagonal bodies and deep folded drapery is framed by paired columns.
A projecting curved architectural canopy and layered pediment concentrate attention on the central niche.
Long gilded rays descend behind the figures, linking the sculptural group with the architectural opening above.
Colored and patterned wall inlays contrast with the pale figures and continue across adjacent architectural surfaces.

association_evidence.supports: Turismo Roma places Santa Maria della Vittoria in Roman Baroque architecture and identifies the Cornaro family chapel as a Bernini commission. It dates the Ecstasy of Saint Teresa sculptural group to 1647–1652 and describes its theatrical setting, including side spectator boxes outside the selected crop.

Turismo Roma describes the Cornaro Chapel’s combination of painting, sculpture, architecture, scenic representation and designed lighting, and reports its 2021 cleaning and consolidation. It notes that the yellow shielding glass is twentieth-century material, probably reproducing Bernini’s original effect.
